Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.

When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. 79	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). An unhandled failure must fault the flow. When you do wire an `error` edge, it must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. Without this, a failed run reports success. See [shared/file-format.md — Implicit error port on action nodes](../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).

Ask before building ([SKILL.md rule #5](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) — dropdown + "Something else"), or state your assumption explicitly and get confirmation. 7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10

12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->

46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
110	
111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
112	
113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118	
119	```bash
120	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
121	```
122	
123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
124	
125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. When solutions already exist and the user chooses "Create a new solution", **ask for the new solution's name** — do not reuse the project name (SKILL.md rule #6). The two names are independent.

127	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
128	
129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```
132	
133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.
136	
137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.

139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:
142	
143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```

160	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.
161	
162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.

168	```

273	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
274	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
275	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.

278	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. 279	
280	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
281	
282	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
283	
284	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
285	
286	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
287	|---|---|---|
288	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
289	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
290	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
291	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
292	
293	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
294	
295	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
296	
297	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
298	
299	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
300	
301	**Or skip the anchoring problem:** `scripts/flow_edit.py apply --plan <file>` parses the file and rewrites the arrays directly, so no `old_string` has to be unique. Put every node, edge, variable, mapping and composite for this turn in one plan and apply it in **one** call — see [SKILL.md — Scripts](../../../SKILL.md#scripts) for the op vocabulary. `Edit` remains the right tool for a small in-place value change you want to show as a diff.
302	
303	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
304	
305	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

14	### Step 1 — Fetch a preliminary connection and query trigger objects

16	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.trigger.<connector-key>.<trigger-name>`) and the operation name from the `registry get` response (`model.context[].operation`).

18	**1a. Get any enabled connection** — needed as `--connection-id` for `triggers objects` below.

20	Discovery call is **always**:

24	```
25	
26	`--all-folders` is mandatory. Without it the CLI returns the active folder only and hides connections in other folders the user can see. Plain `uip is connections list "<connector-key>"` is forbidden for discovery.
27	
28	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules, BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.

36	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
37	```

39	Save the response. It carries three pieces per event object that drive later steps:
40	
41	| Field | Drives | Meaning |
42	|------|--------|---------|
43	| `byoaConnection` | Step 1c | If `true`, only BYOA connections are valid for this event |
44	| `isWebhookUrlVisible` | Step 6b | If `true`, retrieve and present the webhook URL |
45	| **`parameters[]`** | Steps 3 & 4 | Object-, query-, and path-scoped input parameters (e.g. shared mailbox, repo, owner). **NOT the complete event-parameter set** — merge with `EventParameters` from `triggers describe` (Step 1b-2). 51	#### Reading `parameters[]`
52	
53	Each entry is one input field the user supplies when configuring the trigger (e.g., GitHub `repo`, Outlook `parentFolderId`, Slack `channelId`). For each:

55	| Key | Use |
56	|---|---|
57	| `name` | Key inside the `--detail` bucket selected by `type` — see below |
58	| `displayName` | Label when prompting the user for a missing value |
59	| `dataType` | Value type (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, …) |
60	| `required` | Drives Step 4's required-field check |
61	| `reference` | Present → resolve to an ID in Step 3 (`uip is resources run list`) before configure |
62	| `description` | Field hint — surface verbatim when prompting |
63	| `design.position` | `"primary"` indicates a top-level input field; other positions are layout hints — safe to ignore for configure |
64	| `type` | Bucket selector in Step 6's `--detail`: `"query"` → `queryParameters`, `"path"` → `pathParameters`, else → `eventParameters` |

280	## Filter Trees
281	
282	Filters are authored as a **structured tree**, not a string expression. The CLI compiles the tree into a JMESPath `filterExpression` using the same logic Studio Web does, and writes both forms into the flow so the trigger round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
283	
284	### Tree shape
285	
286	```jsonc
287	{
288	  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
289	  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
290	  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
291	    {
292	      "id": "<fieldName>",        // from filterFields.fields[].name
293	      "operator": "<Operator>",   // see operator table below
294	      "value": {
295	        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time
296	        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
297	        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not supported
298	      }
299	    }
300	  ],
301	  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
302	}
303	```
304	
305	A no-op filter — used when the user wants all events to fire the trigger — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
306	
307	### Supported operators
308	
309	| Operator | Meaning | Typical field types |
310	|---|---|---|
311	| `Equals` / `NotEquals` | Exact (in)equality | string, number, boolean |
312	| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | Numeric comparison | number, integer |
313	| `Contains` / `NotContains` | Substring match | string |
314	| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | Prefix / suffix match | string |
315	| `IsEmpty` / `IsNotEmpty` | Value is / is not empty string | string (no `value` needed) |
316	| `Is` / `IsNot` | Boolean is true / false | boolean (no `value` needed) |
317	| `In` / `NotIn` / `IsOneOf` / `IsNotOneOf` | Membership — pass comma-separated values in `value.value` | string, number |
318	| `Before` / `BeforeOrEqual` / `After` / `AfterOrEqual` / `DateTimeEquals` / `DateTimeNotEqual` | Date-time comparison (ISO-8601 strings) | date-time |
319	
320	### Examples
321	
322	**Emails containing "urgent" in the subject:**
323	
324	```json
325	{
326	  "groupOperator": 0,
327	  "index": 0,
328	  "filters": [
329	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
330	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
331	  ]
332	}
333	```
334	
335	**Emails from a specific sender AND subject contains "good day":**
336	
337	```json
338	{
339	  "groupOperator": 0,
340	  "index": 0,
341	  "filters": [
342	    { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
343	      "value": { "value": "boss@example.com", "rawString": "\"boss@example.com\"", "isLiteral": true } },
344	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
345	      "value": { "value": "good day", "rawString": "\"good day\"", "isLiteral": true } }
346	  ]
347	}
348	```
349	
350	**Multiple senders (OR) nested inside an outer AND with a subject match:**
351	
352	```json
353	{
354	  "groupOperator": 0,
355	  "index": 0,
356	  "filters": [
357	    { "id": "subject", "operator": "Contains",
358	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
359	  ],
360	  "groups": [
361	    {
362	      "groupOperator": 1,
363	      "index": 1,
364	      "filters": [
365	        { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
366	          "value": { "value": "a@ex.com", "rawString": "\"a@ex.com\"", "isLiteral": true } },
367	        { "id": "from", "operator": "Equals",
368	          "value": { "value": "b@ex.com", "rawString": "\"b@ex.com\"", "isLiteral": true } }
369	      ]
370	    }
371	  ]
372	}
373	```
374	
375	### How to build a filter tree from `filterFields`
376	
377	1. Run `flow registry get` with `--connection-id` (Step 2) and read the `filterFields.fields` array. Each entry has a `name` (use as the leaf `id`), a `type` (drives operator selection), and an optional `description`.
378	
379	Then follow [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md > Building Filter Trees from filterFields](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#building-filter-trees-from-filterfields) for the rest of the procedure (operator selection, leaf composition, value wrapping), the mandatory-filter contract (connector-mandated values like Gmail folder go on `eventParameters`, never the freeform `filter` tree), and array-shaped field handling.
380	
381	### What NOT to generate
382	
383	| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
384	|---|---|---|
385	| `"filterExpression": "(contains(subject, 'x'))"` | Legacy format — the CLI now rejects `filterExpression` as an input field (see MST-8802). It is *only* an output in the generated `.flow`. | Build a `filter` tree with a `Contains` leaf. |
386	| `"filter": "(subject == 'x')"` | `filter` must be an object, not a string. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
387	| `{ "id": "fields.subject", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `filterFields.fields[].name`. | `{ "id": "subject", ... }` |
388	| `{ "id": "subject", "operator": "contains", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive — use PascalCase. | `"operator": "Contains"` |
389	| `{ "value": "urgent" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
390	| `{ "isLiteral": false, "value": "${var}" }` | Expression values are not yet supported by the CLI port. | Resolve the value first, then pass it as a literal. |
391	| Adding a freeform leaf for a connector-mandated field (e.g. Gmail folder, Slack channelId) | Mandatory filters derived from connector event metadata are emitted automatically by the CLI from `eventParameters` — duplicating them in the freeform tree double-applies the clause. | Set the value through `eventParameters` only; the CLI AND-joins the mandatory JMES clause into the top-level `inputs.detail.filterExpression` (matching SW's `combinedFilterExpression`). It is *not* persisted on `essentialConfiguration` — SW classifies it optional and rebuilds it from input field values on restore. |

442	## Testing Trigger Flows
443	
444	`uip maestro flow debug` works with trigger-based flows. Debug does **not** wait for a live event — it **pulls the most recent matching event** from the connector's lookback window and executes immediately.
445	
446	### How debug works for triggers
447	
448	1. Debug calls the connector's `/events/debug` endpoint with `maxResults=5` and a `startDate` (default: 1 hour ago)
449	2. The connector returns up to 5 matching events from that window, sorted most-recent-first
450	3. The runtime uses `FilterMatches[0]` (the most recent match) as the trigger input
451	4. The flow executes immediately with that event data
452	5. If **no matching events** exist in the lookback window, debug fails with error code `3005` (TriggerNoMatches)
453	
454	```bash
455	uip maestro flow debug . --output json
456	# → Fetches most recent matching event from the past ~1 hour
457	# → Flow executes immediately with that event data
458	```
459	
460	### Polling vs webhook triggers in debug
461	
462	| Trigger mode | Debug support | Behavior |
463	|---|---|---|
464	| `polling` | Supported | Pulls recent events via debug API, executes immediately |
465	| `webhooks` | **Not supported** | Webhook triggers cannot be tested in Studio debug mode — debug requires Orchestrator |
466	
467	> **If the trigger uses `webhooks` event mode**, tell the user that debug is not available for webhook triggers. They must deploy to Orchestrator and test with a real webhook event.
468	
469	### Key differences from manual-trigger debug
470	
471	| Aspect | Manual trigger | Connector trigger (polling) |
472	|---|---|---|
473	| Execution start | Immediate with user-provided inputs | Immediate with most recent matching event |
474	| User action needed | Provide input values | Ensure a matching event exists in the past ~1 hour |
475	| Failure mode | Missing required inputs | No matching events in lookback window (error 3005) |
476	
477	### Pre-debug checklist
478	
479	1. **Verify the connection is healthy** — `uip is connections ping "<id>"`
480	2. **Confirm a matching event exists** — the user should have produced the event (e.g., sent an email, created a Jira issue) within the past hour
481	3. **Check event mode** — if `webhooks`, debug is not supported; inform the user

The CLI drops the unmatched leaf from the compiled `filterExpression` instead of failing | Re-run `registry get --connection-id <id>`, compare every leaf `id` against `filterFields.fields[].name`, then re-run `node configure` with the exact names |

503	| `ElementInstanceId` is empty on the selected connection | Connection is not a BYOA connection, or connector does not support webhooks on this connection type | Verify the trigger requires BYOA (Step 1b `byoaConnection` flag). If `true`, switch to a BYOA connection. |
504	
505	### Debug Tips
506	
507	1. **Always verify the connection is healthy** before debugging trigger issues — run `uip is connections ping "<id>"`
508	2. **`flow validate` does NOT catch trigger-specific issues** — missing event parameters, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime
509	3. **Event parameters with `reference` objects** need resolved IDs, not display names — same as IS activity fields
510	4. **Filters are optional** — omit `filter` from `--detail` if the user wants all events to trigger the flow. Do not invent an "empty" expression.
511	5. **Bindings are auto-managed** — `node configure` creates flow-level bindings; `flow debug`/packaging generates `bindings_v2.json` from them
512	6. **Use `uip maestro flow node remove` to remove the manual trigger** — do NOT use `Edit` to delete the start node. The CLI automatically removes associated edges, orphaned definitions, and regenerates `variables.nodes`. Hand-editing skips these cleanup steps and can leave orphaned references.
513	7. **Check `outputResponseDefinition` before writing downstream expressions** — trigger output field names vary by connector. Do not assume field names like `.text` or `.subject` — verify from the enriched `registry get` response (Step 2)
514	8. **Validate filter field names against `filterFields` yourself** — only field names returned in `filterFields.fields[].name` are valid leaf `id`s in the filter tree, and matching is case-sensitive. The CLI no longer rejects an unknown field at configure time: it drops that leaf from the compiled `filterExpression` and reports Success. A guessed name therefore surfaces as a trigger that fires on events the filter should exclude, not as an error.

2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).

26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.

35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	Add the `error` edge above **only when the requirements say what should happen if the call fails.** With no error edge, a failed call faults the flow — the correct, visible default.
176	
177	When an HTTP node does have an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly. Never set the flag on an HTTP node with no error edge — it suppresses the fault, so a failed call flows on and the run reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
178	
179	```json
180	{
181	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
182	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
183	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
184	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
185	  "targetPort": "input"
186	}
187	```

189	### Debug
190	
191	| Error | Cause | Fix |
192	| --- | --- | --- |
193	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
194	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
195	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
196	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
197	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
198	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
199	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Expected when the requirements specify no fallback. If they do, add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
200	| Flow reports `Completed` but the API call failed | `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` with no handler, or an `error` edge routed into the happy path / the success End node | Remove the flag when there is no error edge; otherwise repoint the error edge at a distinct End node with an error/status output, or at `core.logic.terminate`. See [Do not swallow the failure](../../../../shared/file-format.md#do-not-swallow-the-failure) |
201	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |

2	
3	Shared conventions for the `uip` CLI that apply across **all three capabilities** (Author, Operate, Diagnose). Read this first when invoking any `uip` command — every capability assumes these mechanics.
4	
5	## 1. Resolve the `uip` binary and detect command prefix
6	
7	The `uip` CLI is installed via npm. Resolve the binary (it may not be on PATH in nvm environments) and detect the command namespace.
8	
9	```bash
10	UIP=$(command -v uip 2>/dev/null || echo "$(npm root -g 2>/dev/null | sed 's|/node_modules$||')/bin/uip")
11	CURRENT=$($UIP --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}')
12	```
13	
14	If `uip` is not found at all, install it:
15	
16	```bash
17	npm install -g @uipath/cli@latest
18	```
19	
20	If `npm install -g` fails with a permission error, prompt the user to re-run with appropriate privileges — do not retry automatically.
21	
22	### Command prefix by version
23	
24	| Installed version | Command prefix | Example |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| **≥ 0.3.4** | `uip maestro flow` | `uip maestro flow init MyProject` |
27	| **< 0.3.4** | `uip flow` | `uip flow init MyProject` <!-- uip-check-skip --> |
28	
29	```bash
30	MIN_VERSION="0.3.4"
31	if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$MIN_VERSION" "$CURRENT" | sort -V | head -n1)" = "$MIN_VERSION" ]; then
32	  FLOW_CMD="uip maestro flow"
33	else
34	  FLOW_CMD="uip flow" # <!-- uip-check-skip -->  legacy < 0.3.4 prefix
35	fi
36	echo "Using: $FLOW_CMD (CLI version $CURRENT)"
37	```
38	
39	> **All commands across this skill are written as `uip maestro flow ...` (the ≥ 0.3.4 form).** If version detection above returns < 0.3.4, replace `uip maestro flow` with `uip flow`. Arguments and flags are identical — only the prefix differs. See UiPath/cli#841 for background on the restructuring. <!-- uip-check-skip -->
40	
41	## 2. Always use `--output json`
42	
43	All `uip` commands support structured JSON output. Use `--output json` whenever output is parsed programmatically — every reference doc and recipe in this skill assumes it.
44	
45	```bash
46	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
47	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
48	uip maestro flow instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
49	```
50	
51	> **Anti-pattern: `--format json` does NOT exist.** The flag is `--output json`. Using `--format json` produces `error: unknown option '--format'` and exit code 3 on every `uip` subcommand — not a helpful message pointing at `--output`.
52	
53	The `--localstorage-file` warning that appears in some environments is benign and can be ignored.
54	
55	## 3. Prefer `--output-filter` for extraction
56	
57	When extracting one field or a projection from `uip --output json`, use `--output-filter '<jmespath>'`. The CLI exposes `--output-filter <expression>` as a global flag on every subcommand; it applies a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org/) expression to the `Data` envelope **before** printing. Write expressions starting at `Data` — do **not** prefix them with `Data.`.
58	
59	**Canonical example (broad discovery)** — list all nodes matching a keyword with the standard projection:
60	
61	```bash
62	uip maestro flow registry search slack --output json \
63	  --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
64	```
65	
66	This is the form used in the connector skill — see [Cross-references](#cross-references) below — and is the right starting point when you want to inspect what's available.
67	
68	**Narrow query** — once you know the connector namespace, filter to a single connector's activities:
69	
70	```bash
71	uip maestro flow registry search slack --output json \
72	  --output-filter "[?starts_with(NodeType,'uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-slack.')].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName}"
73	```
74	
75	`registry search` returns `Data` as a **flat array of PascalCase objects** — `NodeType`, `Category`, `DisplayName`, `Description`, `Version`, `Tags`, `AvailableOnTenant`. Not `Data.Nodes`, not lowercase `type`/`category`; those shapes do not exist. Knowing the shape lets you write the right expression on call #1 — which is the actual protection. Do **not** rely on `--output-filter` to *catch* a wrong-shape guess: a syntactically valid expression that simply doesn't match (e.g. `--output-filter "Nodes"` or `"Nodes[*].NodeType"` against the flat array) returns `Data: []` with **exit 0** — the same silent trap as `python3`/`jq` (see the silent-`[]` note below). Only an *invalid* expression fails loudly with exit 3: a syntax error, or a type error such as `keys(@)` on an array.
76	
77	> **Never `head`/`tail`/`grep -m`/pager a discovery query** (`registry search`, `is connectors list`, any `list`/`search`). A row past the cutoff reads exactly like a row that doesn't exist — the same false-absence trap as the silent `[]`, self-inflicted. To check existence, push the predicate into `--output-filter` so the result is *all* matches and already small; cap rows only on data already known complete or already filtered.

79	> ```bash

16	> **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` to set `parentId`. Without it, the node runs outside the loop context and outputs are null. See [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).

20	## Step 2 — Configure the node
21	
22	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …).
